verdict.rationale: GitCafe's own docs describe personal access tokens that work with the REST API and Git over HTTPS, carry only the permissions you grant, and always expire. That covers the permission and expiry parts of the story. Per-repository selection is documented only for MCP connections, a different feature, so it does not count toward PAT repository scoping. Missing for 10: documented restriction of tokens to specific repositories, detail on available permission scopes and choosing a custom expiry date, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create fine-grained access tokens limited to specific repositories, permissions, and an expiry date

citations.quote: with only the permissions you grant. Tokens start with `gct_` and always expire.
A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant.
